summary: Reproduced that Muse Glimmer guided decoding applied the grammar at token position 6, five tokens before the model-written answer channel header ended at position 11. Added detector opt-in metadata and a rollback-safe channel-header state so Muse resumes constraints at the answer body; unchanged detectors still resume immediately after their reasoning terminator.

tests.what_was_measured: Recorded-base behavior first constrained position 6; fixed Muse behavior first constrained position 11, matching the answer body boundary. Raw output is in reports/j-ccd93ff09a48/reproduction.txt.
153 tests and 64 subtests passed, including the reported Muse stream plus independent second-reasoning-channel, fail-safe, rollback/copy, and non-channel boundary cases.
All repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, and applicable registration checks passed for changed source and tests.

gpu_evidence: The defect is a deterministic token-state boundary reproduced without tensor execution. Muse Glimmer 30B weights were not available, so no model-quality or full serving reproduction was claimed; the assigned gfx950 was not relevant to this off-server state-machine validation.
remaining_limitations: Muse Glimmer 30B NVFP4 weights were unavailable, so the reported production placeholder rate and semantic output quality were not independently measured.
No claim is made for GPT-OSS or another channel-framed architecture; only Muse opts into the new boundary metadata.
This change is Python-only and does not require or validate a native FlyDSL rebuild.
